niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on whether you want psychologically oriented shadow work, a structured spiritual tradition, or a mix. These are good starting points from the options I found:

### Shadow work
- **[Engage the Shadow — Jung Platform](https://jungplatform.com/course/engage-the-shadow)** — A Jungian, depth-psychology approach with practical exercises; includes video and audio recordings. A strong pick if you want a thoughtful, expert-led introduction.
- **[Embracing the Shadow — Charlie Morley / Awake Academy](https://www.awakeacademy.org/course/embracing-the-shadow/)** — A self-paced course that covers several aspects of shadow work, including ancestral and sexual shadows. The listing showed unlimited access and a price of £157; check the current price and course details before enrolling.

### Spiritual practice
- **[Ananda Online Courses](https://www.ananda.org/online-courses/)** — Offers meditation courses and practical instruction. Best if you want a regular meditation practice with a defined method.
- **[WCCM Courses](https://wccm.org/courses/)** — Includes a six-week introduction to Christian meditation. A good fit if you’re interested in contemplative practice within a Christian tradition.
- **[InterSpiritual Meditation — Spirituality & Practice](https://www.spiritualityandpractice.com/ecourses/course/view/103/interspiritual-meditation)** — A cross-tradition course covering practices such as mindfulness, gratitude, and compassion; worth considering if you prefer an interfaith approach.
- **[Stanford Continuing Studies: Cultivating Calm](https://continuingstudies.stanford.edu/courses/liberal-arts-and-sciences/cultivating-calm-exploring-spiritual-wellness/20261_REL-89)** — Explores accessible contemplative practices, including mindfulness meditation and poetic reflection. Check the current schedule and enrollment availability.

**Quick picks:** For Jungian shadow work, start with Jung Platform. For a guided meditation routine, look at Ananda or WCCM. For a blend of traditions, consider InterSpiritual Meditation.

Shadow work can bring up difficult emotions. Choose a course that encourages pacing, reflection, and support rather than promising a quick transformation. It’s educational, not a substitute for therapy; if you’re dealing with trauma or significant distress, consider working with a qualified mental-health professional alongside it. Prices and availability can change.
